items.name: Mercury
items.description: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and the closest to the Sun, completing an orbit every 88 Earth days. Its surface is heavily cratered and resembles Earth's Moon, with extreme temperature variations from 427°C during the day to -173°C at night. Mercury has a very thin atmosphere and no moons, making it a challenging environment for exploration. The planet's small size means it has a weak gravitational pull, and it experiences tidal locking effects from the Sun. Despite its harsh conditions, Mercury has been visited by spacecraft like Mariner 10 and Messenger, which have revealed its complex geological history.

items.name: Venus
items.description: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and is often called Earth's twin due to its similar size and composition. It rotates backwards compared to most planets, with a day longer than its year, taking 243 Earth days to rotate once. The planet has a thick, toxic atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, creating a runaway greenhouse effect that makes it the hottest planet in our solar system with surface temperatures around 462°C. Venus is covered in volcanoes and has no moons, with a surface pressure 92 times that of Earth. Despite its inhospitable conditions, Venus has been studied extensively by spacecraft, revealing a complex geology with evidence of past volcanic activity.

items.name: Earth
items.description: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known planet in the universe to harbor life. It has a diverse range of ecosystems, from lush rainforests to arid deserts, supporting millions of species including humans. The planet's atmosphere is composed of 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and trace amounts of other gases, creating the perfect conditions for life. Earth has one natural satellite, the Moon, which helps stabilize its axial tilt and influences ocean tides. The planet's surface is 71% covered by water, with vast oceans that regulate climate and support marine life. Earth's magnetic field protects it from harmful solar radiation, and its moderate temperatures make it habitable.

items.name: Mars
items.description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and is known as the Red Planet due to iron oxide dust that gives its surface a reddish appearance. It has the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, which stands about 13.6 miles high and is three times taller than Mount Everest. Mars has polar ice caps made of water and carbon dioxide ice, and evidence from spacecraft suggests it once had flowing rivers and lakes billions of years ago. The planet has a thin atmosphere and experiences dust storms that can engulf the entire planet for months. Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, and is a prime target for future human exploration due to its potential for past or present life.

items.name: Jupiter
items.description: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and by far the largest planet in our solar system, with a mass more than twice that of all other planets combined. It is a gas giant composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface, and is known for its Great Red Spot, a massive anticyclonic storm larger than Earth that has been raging for at least 400 years. Jupiter acts as a cosmic vacuum cleaner, protecting inner planets from asteroids and comets with its enormous gravitational pull. The planet has at least 95 known moons, including the four largest Galilean moons - Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto - each with unique characteristics. Jupiter's strong magnetic field creates intense radiation belts and auroras, making it a fascinating subject for astronomical study.

items.name: Saturn
items.description: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is famous for its spectacular ring system, which consists of countless small particles of ice and rock orbiting the planet. It is a gas giant with a low density that would allow it to float in water if there were an ocean large enough to contain it. Saturn's rings are divided into thousands of individual ringlets and gaps, with the largest ring extending up to 282,000 kilometers from the planet's center. The planet has at least 146 known moons, with Titan being the largest and having a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane. Saturn's rapid rotation causes it to bulge at the equator, giving it an oblate spheroid shape, and its strong winds create distinctive cloud bands.

items.name: Uranus
items.description: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and is classified as an ice giant, composed mainly of water, methane, and ammonia ices above a possible rocky core. It is unique among planets for rotating on its side, with an axial tilt of 98 degrees, which causes extreme seasonal variations where each pole experiences 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness. Uranus has a faint ring system discovered in 1977 and at least 28 known moons, with the largest being Titania, Oberon, Umbriel, Ariel, and Miranda. The planet's blue-green color comes from methane in its atmosphere, which absorbs red light and reflects blue light. Uranus has the coldest planetary atmosphere in the solar system, with temperatures dropping to -224°C.

items.name: Neptune
items.description: Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet from the Sun, taking 165 Earth years to complete one orbit. It is an ice giant with a dynamic atmosphere featuring the fastest winds in the solar system, reaching speeds up to 2,100 kilometers per hour. Neptune has a Great Dark Spot, a massive storm system similar to Jupiter's Great Red Spot, though it appears and disappears over time. The planet has 16 known moons, with Triton being the largest and unique for orbiting in the opposite direction of Neptune's rotation. Neptune's deep blue color comes from methane in its atmosphere, and it radiates more heat than it receives from the Sun due to its internal heat source. The planet was discovered through mathematical predictions before being observed telescopically in 1846.
